summary.text: A discrete variable has a gap around each value it can take, so it has either a finite or a countably infinite number of permitted values.
Common examples are variables that must be integers, non-negative integers, positive integers, or only 0 and 1.
Their probability distributions can be expressed with probability mass functions, and calculus methods do not readily suit them.

facts.label: Permitted values
facts.value: Finite, or countably infinite in number

facts.label: Common examples
facts.value: Integers, or only the values 0 and 1

facts.label: Dummy variable
facts.value: A 0-1 variable that works as an on/off switch

items.prompt: You count the cars in a parking lot at the top of each hour. Why is that count a discrete variable?

options.label: Each allowed count has a gap around it, with no allowed value between 3 and 4
It can be written down to as many decimal places as you like
It only ever takes small numbers, so it never gets very large
It changes from one hour to the next as time passes

items.explain: A variable is discrete when there is a positive distance to the nearest other permitted value. Whole-number counts fit that.

items.prompt: A researcher gives a person the value 0 if they are in the control group and 1 otherwise. What job does this 0-1 coding do in an equation?

options.label: It measures how far each person is from the group average
It acts as a switch that turns a parameter on or off
It rounds each person's results to the nearest whole number
It shows how many people are in each group

items.explain: A variable allowed only the values 0 and 1 is called a dummy variable, and it works as a switch that assigns two values to different parameters.

items.prompt: A statistician wants to write down the probability of each possible number of customers who walk in on an hour. Which kind of function fits?

options.label: A probability density function
A difference equation
A probability mass function
A differential equation

items.explain: Probability distributions of discrete variables are expressed with probability mass functions. Density functions are for continuous variables.

items.prompt: A savings account is updated once a day, and time is counted in whole days. What kind of equation describes how the balance evolves?

options.label: A differential equation
A probit equation
An instantaneous-rate equation
A difference equation

items.explain: When time is treated as discrete, the evolution of a variable is described by a difference equation. A differential equation goes with time treated as continuous.

items.prompt: A factory can buy only whole machines, never fractions of one. Which kind of problem is choosing how many to buy?

options.label: Integer programming
Continuous optimization
A problem about an instantaneous rate
A problem about a differential equation

items.explain: A variable restricted to integers is discrete, and integer programming is an example of a problem with discrete variables. Continuous optimization is for continuous ones.

items.prompt: A study measures each person with a yes/no symptom check and also with a smooth cognitive score. How are the two variables classed?

options.label: Both are discrete, because the symptom check is
The yes/no check is discrete and the score is continuous
Both are continuous, because the score is
The yes/no check is continuous and the score is discrete

items.explain: A binary measure is discrete and a cognitive performance score is continuous, so this is an example of a mixed model.
